**What I did and why**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a modest long position: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% year over year), with Services up 13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin, lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose to $123.2B from $114.3B, and operating cash flow was a very strong $118.3B. Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) only because of a one-time, non-operating $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid (Ireland) decision — underlying profitability actually improved. The balance sheet remains exceptional ($140.8B in cash, equivalents and marketable securities; $97.3B of term debt; a new $110B buyback authorization with $95.0B repurchased in FY2024 and a $0.25 quarterly dividend). Key watch items are Greater China weakness (net sales −8% to $67.0B), flat iPhone revenue, and regulatory/antitrust pressure on the App Store, which is why I kept the position small rather than aggressive. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed one limit buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 — about 0.1% above market, well inside the mandate — which filled at $223.00 for roughly $9,812. That is within the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, and no cash was moved out of the account (cash remains ample at ~$40,188 of the original $50,000).
